name: Rubber Hose 1930s
summary: Black-and-white 1930s animation: ink figures with elbow-less rubber-hose limbs, white gloves and pie-cut eyes, projected through grainy, scratched film.
description: An early sound-cartoon look in pure ink and four warm greys. Figures are round, bouncy ink shapes with elbow-less rubber-hose limbs, puffy four-finger white gloves, pie-cut eyes and oversized shoes; the whole world, down to the daisies and the cottages, squashes and sways together on a shared 120 bpm beat. Flat grey washes with crisp ink contour lines form the ground, and everything is shown through a projector: silver-sepia grade, grain, scratches, dust, flicker, a jumping gate and rounded, vignetted frame corners. UI panels are dark title cards with double paper rules and Art-Nouveau corner curls.
bestFor: retro top-down action with crowds of characters
nostalgic menus, title screens and trailers
avoidFor: projects that need colour coding to read

difficulty.why: Characters are short lists of ellipses, blobs and stroked quadratic limbs run through a two-pass painter, so outlines come for free and new figures are quick. The craft is in the animation: 8-frame bouncy walks with bowing limbs, contact squash, and syncing props to the beat. The film layer and ground are written once and reused.

technique.resolution: Native display resolution. Sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screenPx/360 * 1.25), 3, 6) canvas px per world unit (8 walk frames, 2 idle, 2 run, 1 recoil for the main character; 6 frames per small/fast creature, 4 for the large one; normal + flash copies, both facings). Ground chunks of 256 units at up to 3 px per unit. The film layer is baked at grain resolution (1 grain px = round(screenH/900*1.3) display px).
technique.summary: Each sprite is a list of parts painted twice: an outline pass strokes and fills every part in ink #16120e at twice the outline weight (one merged silhouette line), then a fill pass paints flat greys, one grey crescent per part and small white shines. Limbs are stroked quadratic curves (rubber hoses) that take part in both passes. A baked film layer (vignette, gate, grain, flicker) is blitted over the finished frame.
technique.linework: One ink colour: #16120e. Outer silhouette 1.0 world unit (stroke width 2.0, half hidden under the fill), inner separation lines 0.5 units, small items 0.55–0.8. Limbs: ink strokes 1.45 (arms) and 1.75 (legs) wide plus the 1.0 outline, round caps. Ground contours: centred ink line 0.8 units at 92% opacity. Round joins everywhere.
technique.shading: Flat fills with at most ONE darker grey crescent per part (the part clipped against itself shifted up-left by 0.4–2.6 units). Black parts stay flat black and get a thin white rim arc (0.5–0.7 units, alpha 0.8) as rubbery shine. No gradients on figures.
technique.lighting: Implied light from the top-left: white shine ellipses top-left, crescents bottom-right. Solid ink drop shadows at 36% opacity under everything. The only glow is a soft white radial halo on street lamps, flickering at 24 fps.
technique.texture: Film grain over the whole picture (white and dark specks, alpha up to 0.21), changing 24 times a second; ground decals are tiny ink tufts, curls, hatch strokes, daisies and pebbles.

paletteRules: No hue at all: ink, four warm greys (#3a342d, #6d665b, #a0988a, #cdc5b5) and two whites. The faint warmth is built into the greys.
Figures read by value: black bodies with pale face masks, white gloves and light shoes on a light-mid grey ground.
White details (gloves, eyes, buttons, petals) are the brightest values on screen and are reserved for small focal shapes.
Large dark areas are rare in the ground (ponds, hummocks) so ink figures never sink into them.
When other styles' elements are shown, the silver-sepia grade desaturates them; the native palette needs no grade.

typography.role: Titles, counters, clock, floating numbers, bar caps
typography.css: font: 400 34px/1.05 'Limelight', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: .06em; color: #efe9dc; text-shadow: 2px 3px 0 #000;
font: 400 21px/1.15 'Rye', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: .02em; color: #efe9dc; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #000;

typography.role: Body copy, labels, hints (typewriter intertitle feel)

world.summary: Flat grey washes like a painted studio background: large soft regions from low-frequency noise, rasterised per pixel with an analytic signed distance (value / gradient) so each region gets a crisp anti-aliased edge, a lighter inner rim band and a centred ink contour line; dark hummocks get a second faint contour ring 5.5 units inside. Tiny ink decals are baked on top.
layers: Base wash #cfc8b9 with a ±4% very-low-frequency brightness tint
Meadow washes #b2aa9a, lighter rim #bfb8a9 (2.4 u), ink contour 0.8 u
Dark hummocks #928a7c, rim #a39b8c (2.8 u), ink contour + faint inner ring at 5.5 u
Winding paths #e4ddcd (zero-contour of noise, even width), rim #d6cebe, ink edges
Ponds #565047 with ink edge, inner ring at 4 u, paper ripple arcs and slate lily pads
Decals: three-stroke ink tufts, spiral curls, hatch clusters, ink-ringed white daisies, outlined pebbles, small dashes

characters.summary: Round ink figures with elbow-less rubber-hose limbs. Main character (~20 u wide, ~36 u tall): a jaunty black cat-fellow with pointed ears, a pale face mask with two pie-cut eyes, a button nose and a wide open grin, a white polka-dot bow tie, slate shorts with two white buttons, white four-finger gloves, a curly tail and big pale shoes. Small creature: a hopping round imp (ink, slate or white body) with horns, white eyes with pie-cut pupils, a toothy grin and an arrow-tipped tail. Fast creature: a wobbly sheet ghost with big pie-cut eyes, worried brows, an O-mouth and two noodle arms reaching forward. Large creature: a big bully with a black head, stubbled jaw, unibrow, bulb nose, derby hat, a striped sweater barrel body, black boots and huge gloved fists.
rules: Limbs are single quadratic curves from joint to hand/foot; bend comes only from moving the control point sideways – never an elbow or knee.
Every hand is a white glove with a rolled cuff, a thumb and two ink stitch lines; every foot is a big oval shoe with a toe-cap line and a white shine.
Eyes are pie-cut: an ink oval with a wedge cut out of its upper front, showing the face colour behind it.
Ink bodies always carry a pale face mask or patch so the face reads on black.
Walk: 8 frames, two bounces per cycle (body 1.8 u up at passing), lifted foot bows its leg forward, arms swing opposite and bow like noodles.
Hit flash replaces every fill with white (ghosts flash to negative ink); the face stays visible in the flash.
Recoil pose: arms flung up, legs splayed, X eyes and an O mouth.

props.summary: Simple inked studio scenery: curly-canopy trees with spiral curls, tall swirled poplars, bare trees whose branches end in curls, cottages whose windows look like sleepy eyes and whose door is a mouth (with curly chimney smoke), tall crooked houses with round attic windows, white picket fences, clumps of smiling daisies, low rolling hill mounds, curly iron street lamps with a soft glow, barrels, crates and spotted toadstools.
rules: Same two-pass painter and ink outline as the figures; greys only, one crescent per part.
Everything dances on one shared beat (120 bpm): squash on the beat (sy −3…8%), sway from beat to beat (base-anchored skew up to 0.09).
Anthropomorphic touches are small: faces in daisies, eye-like windows – never full characters.
Props stand on solid ink drop shadows at 36% opacity.
Wobbly, hand-drawn geometry: fence pickets lean differently, walls are slightly out of square.

effects.name: Projectile
effects.how: An ink eighth note (or beamed pair / sixteenth) with a 0.6 u white halo outline, wobbling ±0.35 rad instead of rotating, followed by three short ink speed lines.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a paper coin with an ash ring and star emboss, spinning by squashing its width (|cos|, min 0.18). Large: a white faceted diamond with ash/fog facets that pulses on the beat and twinkles.

effects.name: Orbiting object
effects.how: A little white bird with a black wing flapping between two frames at 10 fps, bobbing, facing its direction of travel, with a small drop shadow.

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: A jagged white POW burst (11 spikes, fog centre, ink outline) popping 0.5→1.25→0.35 scale over 0.16 s, plus a 4-point white twinkle flying off.

effects.name: Poof burst
effects.how: Curly cloud puffs (white and fog, each with an inner ink spiral) bursting outward and rising, white outlined stars bouncing out with gravity and ink drops splashing; large bursts add an ink-and-white ring and 14 radiating ink rays.

effects.name: Spawn puddle
effects.how: An ink puddle with splatter dots spreads under the ground (outBack), the creature springs out of it with an elastic stretch, then the puddle dries up.

effects.name: Glow-up
effects.how: Ring + rays, eight music notes floating up with a sway, and a fountain of stars.

effects.name: Run
effects.how: Legs turn into the classic spinning wheel of ink motion arcs; speed lines and zip dashes behind, dust puffs on take-off.

atmosphere.summary: A projector look over the finished frame, stepped at 24 frames per second: flicker, grain, dust, scratches, gate weave and a heavy vignette with rounded gate corners – plus a silver-sepia grade for any foreign colour.
rules: Vignette: radial ink gradient 0 → 0.18 → 0.48 → 0.76 from 40% to 102% of the half diagonal; rounded gate corners (radius 7.5% of the height, softly blurred, 94% black).
Grain: per-pixel white/dark specks, alpha up to 0.21, at round(H/900*1.3) px; 3 baked variants that also carry the flicker (−4.5%, 0, +3% brightness).
Every 1/24 s the variant and a ±3 px offset change; the vertical offset doubles as gate weave (about 1 px).
Dust: 0–4 specks or curly hairs per film frame, black or white, alpha 0.55–0.9, never two frames in a row.
Scratches: up to 3 long vertical lines (white or black, alpha 0.16–0.34) that live 14–36 film frames and jitter sideways.
A cue mark (black dot with a pale ring) blinks top-right for 5 frames every 30 s.
Colour grade: 'color' blend of #978c7b at 74% – only needed when other styles' elements are on screen.

ui.summary: Vintage title cards: dark #17130f panels inside an ornamental border-image (double paper rule with concave corners, a corner dot and an Art-Nouveau curl at each corner), Limelight numbers with a hard black drop shadow, Special Elite captions in wide letter-spacing. The top bar is a film strip with sprocket holes and silver frames; the health-style bar is a pill with a paper engraving-hatch fill. Cards pop in with a rubbery squash and wobble like jelly on hover; the overlay behind them is a sunburst of pale rays.

motion: One shared beat drives everything: 120 bpm; pulse q = max(0, cos(phase*PI))^6 (sharp on the beat), sway = cos(beats*PI) (alternates every beat).
Main character walk: cycle = anim*0.2, 8 frames, two contacts per cycle with squash sx 1.06 / sy 0.93; a small dust puff at 70% of steps.
Idle: hands on hips, toe tap on every other beat, body squash 3.5% on the beat.
Small creatures hop: 6 frames, body up 3.2 u at the peak, legs tuck in the air, contact squash 10–12%, rock ±0.08 rad.
Ghosts float 4.5 u up, bob ±1.8 u, wobble their hem and arms through 6 frames at 8 fps, lean into their motion.
Large creature stomps through 4 frames with contact squash 7–8% and an extra beat pulse.
Spawn: elastic stretch out of an ink puddle; removal: stretch up to 140% in the flash colour, then snap flat and vanish into the poof.
Floating numbers: stretch in (sy 1.6 → 1), overshoot sx 1.4, then shrink and fade.
Film effects step at 24 fps regardless of the frame rate.
do: Draw limbs as one bowed curve – exaggerate the bow when a limb swings.
Put a white glove on every hand and a big shoe on every foot.
Cut a wedge out of every pupil (pie eyes).
Give ink bodies a pale face mask so expressions read.
Sync idle props and figures to one beat.
Keep the ground light-mid grey so black figures pop.
Step film effects at 24 fps for an authentic cadence.
Use ornamental title cards with double rules for every UI panel.
dont: Don't add colour – even a single hue breaks the illusion.
Don't draw elbows, knees or tapered realistic limbs.
Don't use soft gradients or glossy highlights on figures.
Don't let grain, dust and scratches get so strong that small figures disappear.
Don't animate props out of sync – the shared beat is the joke.
Don't put dark regions under dense crowds of ink figures.
Don't use modern sans-serif fonts in the UI.
performance: All figures, props, notes, coins, puffs and stars are baked once in init() (~170 canvases incl. flash and mirrored copies); per frame it is only drawImage with transforms, and the beat is computed once per frame. Ground chunks (256 u) are generators: noise on a coarse 4-unit grid, per-pixel signed-distance work only in cells near a region edge, decals baked in. The film layer is baked per screen size (3 variants at grain resolution, ~1 s to build at 1600×900) and costs one drawImage per frame; dust and scratches are a handful of strokes. The 'color' grade pass is a full-screen blend and is skipped when only native elements are on screen. Avoid reading the canvas back (no self-copies for gate weave).
